=== help .
NAME:
  @PROG@ - MinIO Client for object storage and filesystems.

USAGE:
  @PROG@ [FLAGS] COMMAND [COMMAND FLAGS | -h] [ARGUMENTS...]

COMMANDS:
  alias      manage server credentials in configuration file
  admin      manage MinIO servers
  anonymous  manage anonymous access to buckets and objects
  batch      manage batch jobs
  cp         copy objects
  cat        display object contents
  cors       manage bucket CORS configuration
  diff       list differences in object name, size, and date between two buckets
  du         summarize disk usage recursively
  encrypt    manage bucket encryption config
  event      manage object notifications
  find       search for objects
  get        get s3 object to local
  head       display first 'n' lines of an object
  ilm        manage bucket lifecycle
  idp        manage MinIO IDentity Provider server configuration
  legalhold  manage legal hold for object(s)
  ls         list buckets and objects
  mb         make a bucket
  mv         move objects
  mirror     synchronize object(s) to a remote site
  od         measure single stream upload and download
  ping       perform liveness check
  pipe       stream STDIN to an object
  put        upload an object to a bucket
  quota      manage bucket quota
  rm         remove object(s)
  retention  set retention for object(s)
  rb         remove a bucket
  replicate  configure server side bucket replication
  ready      checks if the cluster is ready or not
  sql        run sql queries on objects
  stat       show object metadata
  share      generate URL for temporary access to an object
  tree       list buckets and objects in a tree format
  tag        manage tags for bucket and object(s)
  undo       undo PUT/DELETE operations
  update     update mc to latest release
  version    manage bucket versioning
  watch      listen for object notification events
  
GLOBAL FLAGS:
  --config-dir value, -C value     path to configuration folder (default: "@CONFIG_DIR@") [$MC_CONFIG_DIR]
  --quiet, -q                      disable progress bar display [$MC_QUIET]
  --disable-pager, --dp            disable mc internal pager and print to raw stdout [$MC_DISABLE_PAGER]
  --no-color                       disable color theme [$MC_NO_COLOR]
  --json                           enable JSON lines formatted output [$MC_JSON]
  --debug                          enable debug output [$MC_DEBUG]
  --resolve value                  resolves HOST[:PORT] to an IP address. Example: minio.local:9000=10.10.75.1 [$MC_RESOLVE]
  --insecure                       disable SSL certificate verification [$MC_INSECURE]
  --limit-upload value             limits uploads to a maximum rate in KiB/s, MiB/s, GiB/s. (default: unlimited) [$MC_LIMIT_UPLOAD]
  --limit-download value           limits downloads to a maximum rate in KiB/s, MiB/s, GiB/s. (default: unlimited) [$MC_LIMIT_DOWNLOAD]
  --custom-header value, -H value  add custom HTTP header to the request. 'key:value' format.
  --help, -h                       show help
  --version, -v                    print the version

=== help alias
NAME:
  @PROG@ alias - manage server credentials in configuration file

USAGE:
  @PROG@ alias COMMAND [COMMAND FLAGS | -h] [ARGUMENTS...]

COMMANDS:
  set, s      set a new alias to configuration file
  list, ls    list aliases in configuration file
  remove, rm  remove an alias from configuration file
  import, i   import configuration info to configuration file from a JSON formatted string 
  export, e   export configuration info to stdout
  
FLAGS:
  --config-dir value, -C value     path to configuration folder (default: "@CONFIG_DIR@") [$MC_CONFIG_DIR]
  --quiet, -q                      disable progress bar display [$MC_QUIET]
  --disable-pager, --dp            disable mc internal pager and print to raw stdout [$MC_DISABLE_PAGER]
  --no-color                       disable color theme [$MC_NO_COLOR]
  --json                           enable JSON lines formatted output [$MC_JSON]
  --debug                          enable debug output [$MC_DEBUG]
  --resolve value                  resolves HOST[:PORT] to an IP address. Example: minio.local:9000=10.10.75.1 [$MC_RESOLVE]
  --insecure                       disable SSL certificate verification [$MC_INSECURE]
  --limit-upload value             limits uploads to a maximum rate in KiB/s, MiB/s, GiB/s. (default: unlimited) [$MC_LIMIT_UPLOAD]
  --limit-download value           limits downloads to a maximum rate in KiB/s, MiB/s, GiB/s. (default: unlimited) [$MC_LIMIT_DOWNLOAD]
  --custom-header value, -H value  add custom HTTP header to the request. 'key:value' format.
  --help, -h                       show help

=== help alias set
NAME:
  @PROG@ alias set - set a new alias to configuration file

USAGE:
  @PROG@ alias set ALIAS URL ACCESSKEY SECRETKEY

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Add MinIO service under "myminio" alias. For security reasons turn off bash history momentarily.
     $ set +o history
     $ @PROG@ alias set myminio http://localhost:9000 minio minio123
     $ set -o history
  2. Add MinIO service under "myminio" alias, to use dns style bucket lookup. For security reasons
     turn off bash history momentarily.
     $ set +o history
     $ @PROG@ alias set myminio http://localhost:9000 minio minio123 --api "s3v4" --path "off"
     $ set -o history
  3. Add Amazon S3 storage service under "mys3" alias. For security reasons turn off bash history momentarily.
     $ set +o history
     $ @PROG@ alias set mys3 https://s3.amazonaws.com \
                 BKIKJAA5BMMU2RHO6IBB V8f1CwQqAcwo80UEIJEjc5gVQUSSx5ohQ9GSrr12
     $ set -o history
  4. Add Amazon S3 storage service under "mys3" alias, prompting for keys.
     $ @PROG@ alias set mys3 https://s3.amazonaws.com --api "s3v4" --path "off"
     Enter Access Key: BKIKJAA5BMMU2RHO6IBB
     Enter Secret Key: V8f1CwQqAcwo80UEIJEjc5gVQUSSx5ohQ9GSrr12
  5. Add Amazon S3 storage service under "mys3" alias using piped keys.
     $ set +o history
     $ echo -e "BKIKJAA5BMMU2RHO6IBB\nV8f1CwQqAcwo80UEIJEjc5gVQUSSx5ohQ9GSrr12" | \
                 @PROG@ alias set mys3 https://s3.amazonaws.com --api "s3v4" --path "off"
     $ set -o history

=== help alias import
NAME:
  @PROG@ alias import - import configuration info to configuration file from a JSON formatted string 

USAGE:
  @PROG@ alias import ALIAS ./credentials.json

  Credentials to be imported must be in the following JSON format:
  
  {
    "url": "http://localhost:9000",
    "accessKey": "YJ0RI0F4R5HWY38MD873",
    "secretKey": "OHz5CT7xdMHiXnKZP0BmZ5P4G5UvWvVaxR8gljLG",
    "api": "s3v4",
    "path": "auto"
  }

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Import the provided credentials.json file as 'myminio' to the config:
     $ @PROG@ alias import myminio/ ./credentials.json

  2. Import the credentials through standard input as 'myminio' to the config:
     $ cat credentials.json | @PROG@ alias import myminio/

=== help alias export
NAME:
  @PROG@ alias export - export configuration info to stdout

USAGE:
  @PROG@ alias export ALIAS

  Credentials to be exported will be in the following JSON format:
  
  {
    "url": "http://localhost:9000",
    "accessKey": "YJ0RI0F4R5HWY38MD873",
    "secretKey": "OHz5CT7xdMHiXnKZP0BmZ5P4G5UvWvVaxR8gljLG",
    "api": "s3v4",
    "path": "auto"
  }

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Export the provided 'alias' to credentials.json file:
     $ @PROG@ alias export myminio/ > credentials.json

  2. Export the credentials to standard output and pipe it to import command
     $ @PROG@ alias export alias1/  | mc alias import alias2/

=== help admin user add
NAME:
  @PROG@ admin user add - add a new user

USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin user add TARGET ACCESSKEY SECRETKEY

ACCESSKEY:
  Also called as username.

SECRETKEY:
  Also called as password.

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Add a new user 'foobar' to MinIO server.
     $ set +o history
     $ @PROG@ admin user add myminio foobar foo12345
     $ set -o history

  2. Add a new user 'foobar' to MinIO server, prompting for keys.
     $ @PROG@ admin user add myminio
     Enter Access Key: foobar
     Enter Secret Key: foobar12345

  3. Add a new user 'foobar' to MinIO server using piped keys.
     $ set +o history
     $ echo -e "foobar\nfoobar12345" | @PROG@ admin user add myminio
     $ set -o history

  4. Add a new user 'foobar' to MinIO server, then attach IAM policy "writeonly".
     $ @PROG@ admin user add myminio foobar foo12345 
     $ mc admin policy attach myminio writeonly --user foobar

=== flags admin user disable

--quiet, -q                      disable progress bar display [$MC_QUIET]
--disable-pager, --dp            disable mc internal pager and print to raw stdout [$MC_DISABLE_PAGER]
--no-color                       disable color theme [$MC_NO_COLOR]

--insecure                       disable SSL certificate verification [$MC_INSECURE]
--limit-upload value             limits uploads to a maximum rate in KiB/s, MiB/s, GiB/s. (default: unlimited) [$MC_LIMIT_UPLOAD]

=== help admin user svcacct add
NAME:
  @PROG@ admin user svcacct add - add a new service account

USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin user svcacct add ALIAS ACCOUNT [FLAGS]

ACCOUNT:
  An account could be a regular MinIO user, STS or LDAP user.

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Add a new service account for user 'foobar' to MinIO server with a name and description.
     $ @PROG@ admin user svcacct add myminio foobar --name uploaderKey --description "foobar uploader scripts"

  2. Add a new service account to MinIO server with specified access key and secret key for user 'foobar'.
     $ @PROG@ admin user svcacct add myminio foobar --access-key "myaccesskey" --secret-key "mysecretkey"

  3. Add a new service account to MinIO server with specified access key and random secret key for user 'foobar'.
     $ @PROG@ admin user svcacct add myminio foobar --access-key "myaccesskey"

  4. Add a new service account to MinIO server with specified secret key and random access key for user 'foobar'.
     $ @PROG@ admin user svcacct add myminio foobar --secret-key "mysecretkey"

  5. Add a new service account to MinIO server with specified expiry date in the future for user 'foobar'.
     $ @PROG@ admin user svcacct add myminio foobar --expiry 2023-06-24T10:00:00-07:00

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. List all entities associated with all policies

  2. List all entities associated with the policies 'finteam-policy' and 'mlteam-policy'

  4. List all policies associated with a pair of group entities

  5. List all entities associated with a policy, group and user
     $ @PROG@ admin policy entities play/ \
              --policy finteam-policy --user bobfisher --group consulting

--json                            enable JSON lines formatted output [$MC_JSON]
--debug                           enable debug output [$MC_DEBUG]
--resolve value                   resolves HOST[:PORT] to an IP address. Example: minio.local:9000=10.10.75.1 [$MC_RESOLVE]
--insecure                        disable SSL certificate verification [$MC_INSECURE]
--limit-upload value              limits uploads to a maximum rate in KiB/s, MiB/s, GiB/s. (default: unlimited) [$MC_LIMIT_UPLOAD]
--limit-download value            limits downloads to a maximum rate in KiB/s, MiB/s, GiB/s. (default: unlimited) [$MC_LIMIT_DOWNLOAD]
--custom-header value, -H value   add custom HTTP header to the request. 'key:value' format.
--deployment-id value             deployment id of the site, should be a unique value
--endpoint value                  endpoint for the site
--mode value                      change mode of replication for this target, valid values are ['sync', 'async'].
--bucket-bandwidth value          Set default bandwidth limit for bucket in bytes per second (K,B,G,T for metric and Ki,Bi,Gi,Ti for IEC units)
--disable-ilm-expiry-replication  disable ILM expiry rules replication
--enable-ilm-expiry-replication   enable ILM expiry rules replication
--help, -h                        show help
=== help admin replicate update
NAME:
  @PROG@ admin replicate update - modify endpoint of site participating in site replication

USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin replicate update ALIAS --deployment-id [DEPLOYMENT-ID] --endpoint [NEW-ENDPOINT]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

EXAMPLES:
  1. Edit a site endpoint participating in cluster-level replication:
     $ @PROG@ admin replicate update myminio --deployment-id c1758167-4426-454f-9aae-5c3dfdf6df64 --endpoint https://minio2:9000

  2. Set default bucket bandwidth limit for replication from myminio to the peer cluster with deployment-id c1758167-4426-454f-9aae-5c3dfdf6df64
     $ @PROG@ admin replicate update myminio --deployment-id c1758167-4426-454f-9aae-5c3dfdf6df64 --bucket-bandwidth "2G"

  3. Disable replication of ILM expiry in cluster-level replication:
     $ @PROG@ admin replicate update myminio --disable-ilm-expiry-replication

  4. Enable replication of ILM expiry in cluster-level replication:
     $ @PROG@ admin replicate update myminio --enable-ilm-expiry-replication

USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin replicate status TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

EXAMPLES:

       $ @PROG@ admin replicate status minio1

    2. Display site replication status of buckets across sites
       $ @PROG@ admin replicate status minio1 --buckets

    3. Drill down and view site replication status of bucket "bucket"
       $ @PROG@ admin replicate status minio1 --bucket bucket

    4. Drill down and view site replication status of user "foo"
       $ @PROG@ admin replicate status minio1 --user foo

=== help admin config get
NAME:
  @PROG@ admin config get - interactively retrieve a config key parameters

USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin config get TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  The output includes environment variables set on the server. These cannot be overridden from the client.

  1. Get the current region setting on MinIO server.
     $ @PROG@ admin config get play/ region
     region name=us-east-1

  2. Get the current notification settings for Webhook target on MinIO server
     $ @PROG@ admin config get myminio/ notify_webhook
     notify_webhook endpoint="http://localhost:8080" auth_token= queue_limit=10000 queue_dir="/home/events"

  3. Get the current compression settings on MinIO server
     $ @PROG@ admin config get myminio/ compression
     compression extensions=".txt,.csv" mime_types="text/*"

=== help admin prometheus generate
NAME:
  @PROG@ admin prometheus generate - generates prometheus config

USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin prometheus generate TARGET [METRIC-TYPE]

METRIC-TYPE:
  valid values are
    api-version v2 ['cluster', 'node', 'bucket', 'resource']. defaults to 'cluster' if not specified.
    api-version v3 ["api", "system", "debug", "cluster", "ilm", "audit", "logger", "replication", "notification", "scanner"]. defaults to all if not specified.

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES (v3):
  1. Generate a default prometheus config.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play --api-version v3

  2. Generate prometheus config for api metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play api --api-version v3

  3. Generate prometheus config for api metrics of bucket 'mybucket'.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play api --bucket mybucket --api-version v3

  4. Generate prometheus config for system metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play system --api-version v3

  5. Generate prometheus config for debug metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play debug --api-version v3

  6. Generate prometheus config for cluster metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play cluster --api-version v3

  7. Generate prometheus config for ilm metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play ilm --api-version v3

  8. Generate prometheus config for audit metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play audit --api-version v3

  9. Generate prometheus config for logger metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play logger --api-version v3

  10. Generate prometheus config for replication metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play replication --api-version v3

  11. Generate prometheus config for replication metrics of bucket 'mybucket'.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play replication --bucket mybucket --api-version v3

  12. Generate prometheus config for notification metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play notification --api-version v3

  13. Generate prometheus config for scanner metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play scanner --api-version v3

EXAMPLES (v2):
  1. Generate a default prometheus config.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play

  2. Generate prometheus config for node metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play node

  3. Generate prometheus config for bucket metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play bucket

  4. Generate prometheus config for resource metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play resource

  5. Generate prometheus config for cluster metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus generate play cluster

NAME:
  @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics - print prometheus metrics
USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics TARGET [METRIC-TYPE]

METRIC-TYPE:
  valid values are
    api-version v2 ['cluster', 'node', 'bucket', 'resource']. defaults to 'cluster' if not specified.
    api-version v3 ["api", "system", "debug", "cluster", "ilm", "audit", "logger", "replication", "notification", "scanner"]. defaults to all if not specified.

     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play api --api-version v3

     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play api --bucket mybucket --api-version v3

  3. System metrics
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play system --api-version v3

  4. Debug metrics
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play debug --api-version v3

  5. Cluster metrics
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play cluster --api-version v3

  6. ILM metrics
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play ilm --api-version v3

  7. Audit metrics
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play audit --api-version v3

  8. Logger metrics
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play logger --api-version v3

  9. Replication metrics
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play replication --api-version v3

  10. Replication metrics for the bucket 'mybucket'
      $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play replication --bucket mybucket --api-version v3

  11. Notification metrics
      $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play notification --api-version v3

  12. Scanner metrics
      $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play scanner --api-version v3

EXAMPLES (v2):
  1. Metrics reported cluster wide.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play

     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play node

  3. Metrics reported at bucket level.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play bucket

  4. Resource metrics.
     $ @PROG@ admin prometheus metrics play resource

--debug                          enable debug output [$MC_DEBUG]
--resolve value                  resolves HOST[:PORT] to an IP address. Example: minio.local:9000=10.10.75.1 [$MC_RESOLVE]
--insecure                       disable SSL certificate verification [$MC_INSECURE]
--limit-upload value             limits uploads to a maximum rate in KiB/s, MiB/s, GiB/s. (default: unlimited) [$MC_LIMIT_UPLOAD]
--limit-download value           limits downloads to a maximum rate in KiB/s, MiB/s, GiB/s. (default: unlimited) [$MC_LIMIT_DOWNLOAD]

=== help admin scanner trace
NAME:
  @PROG@ admin scanner trace - show trace for MinIO scanner operations

USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin scanner trace [FLAGS] TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

UNITS
  --filter-size flags use with --filter-response or --filter-request accept human-readable case-insensitive number
  suffixes such as "k", "m", "g" and "t" referring to the metric units KB,
  MB, GB and TB respectively. Adding an "i" to these prefixes, uses the IEC
  units, so that "gi" refers to "gibibyte" or "GiB". A "b" at the end is
  also accepted. Without suffixes the unit is bytes.

EXAMPLES:
  1. Show scanner trace for MinIO server
     $ @PROG@ admin scanner trace myminio

  2. Show scanner trace for a specific path
    $ @PROG@ admin scanner trace --path my-bucket/my-prefix/* myminio

  3. Show trace for only ScanObject operations
    $ @PROG@ admin scanner trace --funcname=scanner.ScanObject myminio

  4. Avoid printing replication related S3 requests
    $ @PROG@ admin scanner trace --request-header '!X-Minio-Source' myminio

  5. Show trace only for ScanObject operations request bytes greater than 1MB
    $ @PROG@ admin scanner trace --filter-request --filter-size 1MB myminio

  6. Show trace only for ScanObject operations response bytes greater than 1MB
    $ @PROG@ admin scanner trace --filter-response --filter-size 1MB myminio
  
  7. Show trace only for requests operations duration greater than 5ms
    $ @PROG@ admin scanner trace --response-duration 5ms myminio

=== flags admin trace
--verbose, -v                    print verbose trace
--all, -a                        trace all call types
--call value                     trace only matching call types. See CALL TYPES below for list. (default: s3)
--status-code value              trace only matching status code
--method value                   trace only matching HTTP method
--funcname value                 trace only matching func name
--path value                     trace only matching path
--node value                     trace only matching servers
--request-header value           trace only matching request headers
--request-query value            trace only matching request queries
--errors, -e                     trace only failed requests
--stats                          print statistical summary of all the traced calls
--filter-request                 trace calls only with request bytes greater than this threshold, use with filter-size
--filter-response                trace calls only with response bytes greater than this threshold, use with filter-size
--response-duration 5ms          trace calls only with response duration greater than this threshold (e.g. 5ms) (default: 0s)
--filter-size value              filter size, use with filter (see UNITS)
--in value                       read previously saved json from file and replay

=== help admin trace
NAME:
  @PROG@ admin trace - Show HTTP call trace for all incoming and internode on MinIO

USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin trace [FLAGS] TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
CALL TYPES:
  batch-expiration:    Trace Batch Expiration (alias: bexp)
  batch-keyrotation:   Trace Batch KeyRotation (alias: brot)
  batch-replication:   Trace Batch Replication (alias: brep)
  bootstrap:           Trace Bootstrap operations
  decommission:        Trace Decommission operations (alias: decom)
  ftp:                 Trace FTP operations
  healing:             Trace Healing operations (alias: heal)
  ilm:                 Trace ILM operations
  internal:            Trace Internal RPC calls
  os:                  Trace Operating System calls
  rebalance:           Trace Server Pool Rebalancing operations
  replication-resync:  Trace Replication Resync operations (alias: resync)
  s3:                  Trace S3 API calls
  scanner:             Trace Scanner calls
  storage:             Trace Storage calls

UNITS
  --filter-size flags use with --filter-response or --filter-request accept human-readable case-insensitive number
  suffixes such as "k", "m", "g" and "t" referring to the metric units KB,
  MB, GB and TB respectively. Adding an "i" to these prefixes, uses the IEC
  units, so that "gi" refers to "gibibyte" or "GiB". A "b" at the end is
  also accepted. Without suffixes the unit is bytes.

EXAMPLES:
  1. Show verbose console trace for MinIO server
     $ @PROG@ admin trace -v -a myminio

  2. Show trace only for failed requests for MinIO server
    $ @PROG@ admin trace -v -e myminio

  3. Show verbose console trace for requests with '503' status code
    $ @PROG@ admin trace -v --status-code 503 myminio

  4. Show console trace for a specific path
    $ @PROG@ admin trace --path my-bucket/my-prefix/* myminio

  5. Show console trace for requests with '404' and '503' status code
    $ @PROG@ admin trace --status-code 404 --status-code 503 myminio
  
  6. Show trace only for requests bytes greater than 1MB
    $ @PROG@ admin trace --filter-request --filter-size 1MB myminio

  7. Show trace only for response bytes greater than 1MB
    $ @PROG@ admin trace --filter-response --filter-size 1MB myminio
  
  8. Show trace only for requests operations duration greater than 5ms
     $ @PROG@ admin trace --response-duration 5ms myminio

     $ @PROG@ admin logs myminio
  2. Show last 5 log entries for node 'node1' for a MinIO server with alias 'myminio'
     $ @PROG@ admin logs --last 5 myminio node1
  3. Show application errors in logs for a MinIO server with alias 'myminio'
     $ @PROG@ admin logs --type application myminio

=== help admin accesskey list
NAME:
  @PROG@ admin accesskey list - list access key pairs for builtin users

USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin accesskey list [FLAGS] TARGET [DN...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Get list of all builtin users and associated access keys in local server
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey list local/ --all

  2. Get list of access keys for the authenticated user in local server
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey list local/ --self

  3. Get list of builtin users in local server
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey list local/ --all --users-only

  4. Get list of all builtin users and associated temporary access keys in play server (if admin)
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey list play/ --temp-only

  5. Get list of access keys associated with user 'foobar'
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey list play/ foobar

  6. Get list of access keys associated with users 'foobar' and 'tester'
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey list play/ foobar tester

  7. Get all users and access keys if admin, else get authenticated user and associated access keys
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey list local/

=== help admin accesskey create
NAME:
  @PROG@ admin accesskey create - create access key pairs for users

USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin accesskey create [FLAGS] [TARGET]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Create a new access key pair with the same policy as the authenticated user
     $ @PROG@ admin accesskey create myminio/

  2. Create a new access key pair with custom access key and secret key
     $ @PROG@ admin accesskey create myminio/ --access-key myaccesskey --secret-key mysecretkey

  3. Create a new access key pair for user 'tester' that expires in 1 day
     $ @PROG@ admin accesskey create myminio/ tester --expiry-duration 24h

  4. Create a new access key pair for authenticated user that expires on 2025-01-01
     $ @PROG@ admin accesskey create --expiry 2025-01-01

  5. Create a new access key pair for user 'tester' with a custom policy
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey create myminio/ tester --policy /path/to/policy.json

  6. Create a new access key pair for user 'tester' with a custom name and description
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey create myminio/ tester --name "Tester's Access Key" --description "Access key for tester"

=== help admin accesskey sts-revoke
NAME:
  @PROG@ admin accesskey sts-revoke - revokes all STS accounts or specified types for the specified user

USAGE:
  @PROG@ admin accesskey sts-revoke ALIAS USER [--all | --token-type TOKEN_TYPE]

  Exactly one of --all or --token-type must be specified.

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Revoke all STS accounts for user "user1"
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey sts-revoke myminio user1 --all

  2. Revoke STS accounts of a token type "app-1" for user "user1"
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey sts-revoke myminio user1 --token-type app-1

  3. Revoke all STS accounts for the authenticated user
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey sts-revoke myminio --self

  4. Revoke STS accounts of a token type "app-1" for the authenticated user
   $ @PROG@ admin accesskey sts-revoke myminio --self --token-type app-1

=== help anonymous
Name:
  @PROG@ anonymous - manage anonymous access to buckets and objects

USAGE:
  @PROG@ anonymous [FLAGS] set PERMISSION TARGET
  @PROG@ anonymous [FLAGS] set-json FILE TARGET
  @PROG@ anonymous [FLAGS] get TARGET
  @PROG@ anonymous [FLAGS] get-json TARGET
  @PROG@ anonymous [FLAGS] list TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
PERMISSION:
  Allowed policies are: [private, public, download, upload].

FILE:
  A valid S3 anonymous JSON filepath.

EXAMPLES:
  1. Set bucket to "download" on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ @PROG@ anonymous set download s3/mybucket

  2. Set bucket to "public" on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ @PROG@ anonymous set public s3/shared

  3. Set bucket to "upload" on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ @PROG@ anonymous set upload s3/incoming

  4. Set anonymous to "public" for bucket with prefix on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ @PROG@ anonymous set public s3/public-commons/images

  5. Set a custom prefix based bucket anonymous on Amazon S3 cloud storage using a JSON file.
     $ @PROG@ anonymous set-json /path/to/anonymous.json s3/public-commons/images 

  6. Get bucket permissions.
     $ @PROG@ anonymous get s3/shared

  7. Get bucket permissions in JSON format.
     $ @PROG@ anonymous get-json s3/shared

  8. List policies set to a specified bucket.
     $ @PROG@ anonymous list s3/shared

  9. List public object URLs recursively.
     $ @PROG@ anonymous --recursive links s3/shared/

=== flags cp
--rewind value                     roll back object(s) to current version at specified time
--version-id value, --vid value    select an object version to copy
--recursive, -r                    copy recursively
--older-than value                 copy objects older than value in duration string (e.g. 7d10h31s)
--newer-than value                 copy objects newer than value in duration string (e.g. 7d10h31s)
--storage-class value, --sc value  set storage class for new object(s) on target
--attr value                       add custom metadata for the object
--preserve, -a                     preserve filesystem attributes (mode, ownership, timestamps)
--disable-multipart                disable multipart upload feature
--tags value                       apply one or more tags to the uploaded objects
--retention-mode value             retention mode to be applied on the object (governance, compliance)
--retention-duration value         retention duration for the object in d days or y years
--legal-hold value                 apply legal hold to the copied object (on, off)
--zip                              Extract from remote zip file (MinIO server source only)
--max-workers value                maximum number of concurrent copies (default: autodetect) (default: 0)
--checksum value                   Add checksum to uploaded object. Values: CRC64NVME, CRC32, CRC32C, SHA1 or SHA256. Requires server trailing headers (AWS, MinIO)
--enc-c value                      encrypt/decrypt objects using client provided keys. (multiple keys can be provided) Formats: RawBase64 or Hex.
--enc-kms value                    encrypt/decrypt objects using specific server-side encryption keys. (multiple keys can be provided) [$MC_ENC_KMS]
--enc-s3 value                     encrypt/decrypt objects using server-side default keys and configurations. (multiple keys can be provided). [$MC_ENC_S3]
--config-dir value, -C value       path to configuration folder (default: "@CONFIG_DIR@") [$MC_CONFIG_DIR]
--quiet, -q                        disable progress bar display [$MC_QUIET]
--disable-pager, --dp              disable mc internal pager and print to raw stdout [$MC_DISABLE_PAGER]
--no-color                         disable color theme [$MC_NO_COLOR]
--json                             enable JSON lines formatted output [$MC_JSON]
--debug                            enable debug output [$MC_DEBUG]
--resolve value                    resolves HOST[:PORT] to an IP address. Example: minio.local:9000=10.10.75.1 [$MC_RESOLVE]
--insecure                         disable SSL certificate verification [$MC_INSECURE]
--limit-upload value               limits uploads to a maximum rate in KiB/s, MiB/s, GiB/s. (default: unlimited) [$MC_LIMIT_UPLOAD]
--limit-download value             limits downloads to a maximum rate in KiB/s, MiB/s, GiB/s. (default: unlimited) [$MC_LIMIT_DOWNLOAD]
--custom-header value, -H value    add custom HTTP header to the request. 'key:value' format.

=== help cp
NAME:
  @PROG@ cp - copy objects

USAGE:
  @PROG@ cp [FLAGS] SOURCE [SOURCE...] TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES:
  MC_ENC_KMS: KMS encryption key in the form of (alias/prefix=key).
  MC_ENC_S3: S3 encryption key in the form of (alias/prefix=key).

EXAMPLES:
  01. Copy a list of objects from local file system to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ cp Music/*.ogg s3/jukebox/

  02. Copy a folder recursively from MinIO cloud storage to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ cp --recursive play/mybucket/myfolder/ s3/mybucket/

  03. Copy multiple local folders recursively to MinIO cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ cp --recursive backup/2014/ backup/2015/ play/archive/

  04. Copy a bucket recursively from aliased Amazon S3 cloud storage to local filesystem on Windows.
      $ @PROG@ cp --recursive s3\documents\2014\ C:\Backups\2014

  05. Copy files older than 7 days and 10 hours from MinIO cloud storage to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ cp --older-than 7d10h play/mybucket/myfolder/ s3/mybucket/

  06. Copy files newer than 7 days and 10 hours from MinIO cloud storage to a local path.
      $ @PROG@ cp --newer-than 7d10h play/mybucket/myfolder/ ~/latest/

  07. Copy an object with name containing unicode characters to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ cp 本語 s3/andoria/

  08. Copy a local folder with space separated characters to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ cp --recursive 'workdir/documents/May 2014/' s3/miniocloud

  09. Copy a folder with encrypted objects recursively from Amazon S3 to MinIO cloud storage using s3 encryption.
      $ @PROG@ cp --recursive --enc-s3 "s3/documents" --enc-s3 "myminio/documents" s3/documents/ myminio/documents/

  10. Copy a folder with encrypted objects recursively from Amazon S3 to MinIO cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ cp --recursive --enc-c "s3/documents/=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5MDA" --enc-c "myminio/documents/=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5BBB" s3/documents/ myminio/documents/

  11. Copy a list of objects from local file system to MinIO cloud storage with specified metadata, separated by ";"
      $ @PROG@ cp --attr "key1=value1;key2=value2" Music/*.mp4 play/mybucket/

  12. Copy a folder recursively from MinIO cloud storage to Amazon S3 cloud storage with Cache-Control and custom metadata, separated by ";".
      $ @PROG@ cp --attr "Cache-Control=max-age=90000,min-fresh=9000;key1=value1;key2=value2" --recursive play/mybucket/myfolder/ s3/mybucket/

  13. Copy a text file to an object storage and assign REDUCED_REDUNDANCY storage-class to the uploaded object.
      $ @PROG@ cp --storage-class REDUCED_REDUNDANCY myobject.txt play/mybucket

  14. Copy a text file to an object storage and preserve the file system attribute as metadata.
      $ @PROG@ cp -a myobject.txt play/mybucket

  15. Copy a text file to an object storage with object lock mode set to 'GOVERNANCE' with retention duration 1 day.
      $ @PROG@ cp --retention-mode governance --retention-duration 1d locked.txt play/locked-bucket/

  16. Copy a text file to an object storage with legal-hold enabled.
      $ @PROG@ cp --legal-hold on locked.txt play/locked-bucket/

  17. Copy a text file to an object storage and disable multipart upload feature.
      $ @PROG@ cp --disable-multipart myobject.txt play/mybucket

  18. Roll back 10 days in the past to copy the content of 'mybucket'
      $ @PROG@ cp --rewind 10d -r play/mybucket/ /tmp/dest/

  19. Set tags to the uploaded objects
      $ @PROG@ cp -r --tags "category=prod&type=backup" ./data/ play/another-bucket/

=== help cat
NAME:
  @PROG@ cat - display object contents

USAGE:
  @PROG@ cat [FLAGS] TARGET [TARGET...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

EXAMPLES:
  1. Stream an object from Amazon S3 cloud storage to mplayer standard input.
     $ @PROG@ cat s3/mysql-backups/kubecon-mysql-operator.mpv | mplayer -

  2. Concatenate contents of file1.txt and stdin to standard output.
     $ @PROG@ cat file1.txt - > file.txt

  3. Concatenate multiple files to one.
     $ @PROG@ cat part.* > complete.img

  4. Save an encrypted object from Amazon S3 cloud storage to a local file.
     $ @PROG@ cat --enc-c "play/my-bucket/=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5MDA" s3/mysql-backups/backups-201810.gz > /mnt/data/recent.gz

  5. Display the content of encrypted object. In case the encryption key contains non-printable character like tab, pass the
     base64 encoded string as key.
     $ @PROG@ cat --enc-c "play/my-bucket/=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5MDA" play/my-bucket/my-object

  6. Display the content of an object 10 days earlier
     $ @PROG@ cat --rewind 10d play/my-bucket/my-object

  7. Display the content of a particular object version
     $ @PROG@ cat --vid "3ddac055-89a7-40fa-8cd3-530a5581b6b8" play/my-bucket/my-object

USAGE:
  @PROG@ diff [FLAGS] SOURCE TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
DESCRIPTION:
  Diff only calculates differences in object name, size and time. It *DOES NOT* compare objects' contents.

LEGEND:
  < - object is only in source.
  > - object is only in destination.
  ! - newer object is in source.

EXAMPLES:
  1. Compare a local folder with a folder on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ @PROG@ diff ~/Photos s3/mybucket/Photos

  2. Compare two folders on a local filesystem.
     $ @PROG@ diff ~/Photos /Media/Backup/Photos

@FLAGS:2@

@FLAGS:2@

  4. Enable bucket notification for Replication and ILM transition events to a specific ARN
    $ @PROG@ event add myminio/mysourcebucket arn:aws:sqs:us-west-2:444455556666:your-queue --event replica,ilm

=== help find
NAME:
  @PROG@ find - search for objects

USAGE:
  @PROG@ find [FLAGS] TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
UNITS
  --smaller, --larger flags accept human-readable case-insensitive number
  suffixes such as "k", "m", "g" and "t" referring to the metric units KB,
  MB, GB and TB respectively. Adding an "i" to these prefixes, uses the IEC
  units, so that "gi" refers to "gibibyte" or "GiB". A "b" at the end is
  also accepted. Without suffixes the unit is bytes.

  --older-than, --newer-than flags accept the string for days, hours and minutes 
  i.e. 1d2h30m states 1 day, 2 hours and 30 minutes.

FORMAT
  Support string substitutions with special interpretations for following keywords.
  Keywords supported if target is filesystem or object storage:

     {}        --> Substitutes to full path.
     {base}    --> Substitutes to basename of path.
     {dir}     --> Substitutes to dirname of the path.
     {size}    --> Substitutes to object size of the path.
     {time}    --> Substitutes to object modified time of the path.
     {version} --> Substitutes to object version identifier.

  Keywords supported if target is object storage:

     {url} --> Substitutes to a shareable URL of the path.

EXAMPLES:
  01. Find all "foo.jpg" in all buckets under "s3" account.
      $ @PROG@ find s3 --name "foo.jpg"

  02. Find all objects with ".txt" extension under "s3/mybucket".
      $ @PROG@ find s3/mybucket --name "*.txt"

  03. Find only the object names without the directory component under "s3/mybucket".
      $ @PROG@ find s3/mybucket --name "*" -print {base}

  04. Find all images with ".jpg" extension under "s3/photos", prefixed with "album".
      $ @PROG@ find s3/photos --name "*.jpg" --path "*/album*/*"

  05. Find all images with ".jpg", ".png", and ".gif" extensions, using regex under "s3/photos".
      $ @PROG@ find s3/photos --regex "(?i)\.(jpg|png|gif)$"

  06. Find all images with ".jpg" extension under "s3/bucket" and copy to "play/bucket" *continuously*.
      $ @PROG@ find s3/bucket --name "*.jpg" --watch --exec "mc cp {} play/bucket"

  07. Find and generate public URLs valid for 7 days, for all objects between 64 MB, and 1 GB in size under "s3" account.
      $ @PROG@ find s3 --larger 64MB --smaller 1GB --print {url}

  08. Find all objects created in the last week under "s3/bucket".
      $ @PROG@ find s3/bucket --newer-than 7d

  09. Find all objects which were created are older than 2 days, 5 hours and 10 minutes and exclude the ones with ".jpg"
      extension under "s3".
      $ @PROG@ find s3 --older-than 2d5h10m --ignore "*.jpg"

  10. List all objects up to 3 levels sub-directory deep under "s3/bucket".
      $ @PROG@ find s3/bucket --maxdepth 3

  11. Copy all versions of all objects in bucket in the local machine
      $ @PROG@ find s3/bucket --versions --exec "mc cp --version-id {version} {} /tmp/dir/{}.{version}"

NAME:
  @PROG@ head - display first 'n' lines of an object

USAGE:
  @PROG@ head [FLAGS] TARGET [TARGET...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

NOTE:
  '@PROG@ head' automatically decompresses 'gzip', 'bzip2' compressed objects.

EXAMPLES:

     $ @PROG@ head -n 1 s3/csv-data/population.csv.gz

  2. Display only first line from server encrypted object on Amazon S3.
     $ @PROG@ head -n 1 --enc-c 's3/csv-data=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5MDA' s3/csv-data/population.csv

     $ @PROG@ head --enc-c "s3/json-data=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5MDA"  s3/json-data/population.json

  4. Display the first lines of a specific object version.
     $ @PROG@ head --version-id "3ddac055-89a7-40fa-8cd3-530a5581b6b8" s3/json-data/population.json

=== help ilm rule add
NAME:
  @PROG@ ilm rule add - add a lifecycle configuration rule for a bucket

USAGE:
  @PROG@ ilm rule add [COMMAND FLAGS] TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
DESCRIPTION:
  Add a lifecycle configuration rule.

EXAMPLES:
  1. Add a lifecycle rule with a transition and a noncurrent version transition action for objects with prefix doc/ whose size is greater than 1MiB in mybucket.
     Tiers must exist in MinIO. Use existing tiers or add new tiers.

     $ mc ilm tier add minio myminio MINIOTIER-1 --endpoint https://warm-minio-1.com \
         --access-key ACCESSKEY --secret-key SECRETKEY --bucket bucket1 --prefix prefix1

     $ @PROG@ ilm rule add --prefix "doc/" --size-gt 1MiB --transition-days "90" --transition-tier "MINIOTIER-1" \
         --noncurrent-transition-days "45" --noncurrent-transition-tier "MINIOTIER-1" \
         myminio/mybucket/

  2. Add a lifecycle rule with an expiration action for all objects in mybucket.
     $ @PROG@ ilm rule add --expire-days "200" myminio/mybucket

  3. Add a lifecycle rule with an expiration and a noncurrent version expiration action for all objects with prefix doc/ in mybucket.
     $ @PROG@ ilm rule add --prefix "doc/" --expire-days "300" --noncurrent-expire-days "100" \
          myminio/mybucket/

--prefix value                      object prefix
--tags value                        key value pairs of the form '<key1>=<value1>&<key2>=<value2>&<key3>=<value3>'
--size-lt value                     objects with size less than this value will be selected for the lifecycle action
--size-gt value                     objects with size greater than this value will be selected for the lifecycle action
--expire-days value                 number of days to expire
--expire-delete-marker              expire zombie delete markers
--transition-days value             number of days to transition
--transition-tier value             remote tier name to transition

--noncurrent-transition-days value  number of days to transition noncurrent versions (default: 0)
--noncurrent-transition-tier value  remote tier name to transition
--expire-all-object-versions        expire all object versions
--config-dir value, -C value        path to configuration folder (default: "@CONFIG_DIR@") [$MC_CONFIG_DIR]

@FLAGS:2@
  
DESCRIPTION:
  Modify a lifecycle configuration rule with given id.

EXAMPLES:

     $ @PROG@ ilm rule edit --id "rHTY.a123" --expiry-date "2020-09-17" s3/mybucket

  2. Modify the expiration and transition days for an existing rule with id "hGHKijqpo123".
     $ @PROG@ ilm rule edit --id "hGHKijqpo123" --expiry-days "300" \
          --transition-days "200" --storage-class "GLACIER" s3/mybucket

  3. Disable the rule with id "rHTY.a123".
     $ @PROG@ ilm rule edit --id "rHTY.a123" --disable s3/mybucket

=== help ilm rule remove
NAME:
  @PROG@ ilm rule remove - remove (if any) existing lifecycle configuration rule

USAGE:
  @PROG@ ilm rule remove [FLAGS] TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
DESCRIPTION:
  Remove a lifecycle configuration rule for the bucket by ID, optionally you can remove
  all the lifecycle rules on a bucket with '--all --force' option.

EXAMPLES:
  1. Remove the lifecycle management configuration rule given by ID "bgrt1ghju" for mybucket on alias 'myminio'. ID is case sensitive.
     $ @PROG@ ilm rule remove --id "bgrt1ghju" myminio/mybucket

  2. Remove ALL the lifecycle management configuration rules for mybucket on alias 'myminio'.
     Because the result is complete removal, the use of --force flag is enforced.
     $ @PROG@ ilm rule remove --all --force myminio/mybucket

=== help ilm tier add
NAME:
  @PROG@ ilm tier add - add a new remote tier target

USAGE:
  @PROG@ ilm tier add TYPE ALIAS NAME [FLAGS]

TYPE:
  Transition objects to supported cloud storage backend tier. Supported values are minio, s3, azure and gcs.

NAME:
  Name of the remote tier target. e.g WARM-TIER

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Configure a new remote tier which transitions objects to a bucket in a MinIO deployment:
     $ @PROG@ ilm tier add minio myminio WARM-MINIO-TIER --endpoint https://warm-minio.com \
        --access-key ACCESSKEY --secret-key SECRETKEY --bucket mybucket --prefix myprefix/

  2. Configure a new remote tier which transitions objects to a bucket in Azure Blob Storage:
     $ @PROG@ ilm tier add azure myminio AZTIER --account-name ACCOUNT-NAME --account-key ACCOUNT-KEY \
        --bucket myazurebucket --prefix myazureprefix/

  3. Configure a new remote tier which transitions objects to a bucket in AWS S3 with STANDARD storage class:
     $ @PROG@ ilm tier add s3 myminio S3TIER --endpoint https://s3.amazonaws.com \
        --access-key ACCESSKEY --secret-key SECRETKEY --bucket mys3bucket --prefix mys3prefix/ \
        --storage-class "STANDARD" --region us-west-2

  4. Configure a new remote tier which transitions objects to a bucket in Google Cloud Storage:
     $ @PROG@ ilm tier add gcs myminio GCSTIER --credentials-file /path/to/credentials.json \
        --bucket mygcsbucket  --prefix mygcsprefix/

=== help ilm restore
NAME:
  @PROG@ ilm restore - restore archived objects

USAGE:
  @PROG@ ilm restore TARGET

DESCRIPTION:
  Restore a copy of one or more objects from its remote tier. This copy automatically expires
  after the specified number of days (Default 1 day).

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

EXAMPLES:
  1. Restore one specific object
     $ @PROG@ ilm restore myminio/mybucket/path/to/object

  2. Restore a specific object version
     $ @PROG@ ilm restore --vid "CL3sWgdSN2pNntSf6UnZAuh2kcu8E8si" myminio/mybucket/path/to/object

  3. Restore all objects under a specific prefix
     $ @PROG@ ilm restore --recursive myminio/mybucket/dir/

  4. Restore all objects with all versions under a specific prefix
     $ @PROG@ ilm restore --recursive --versions myminio/mybucket/dir/

  5. Restore an SSE-C encrypted object.
     $ @PROG@ ilm restore --enc-c "myminio/mybucket/=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5MDA" myminio/mybucket/myobject.txt

NAME:
  @PROG@ idp openid add - Create an OpenID IDP server configuration

USAGE:
  @PROG@ idp openid add TARGET [CFG_NAME] [CFG_PARAMS...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Create a default OpenID IDP configuration (CFG_NAME is omitted).
     $ @PROG@ idp openid add play/ \
          client_id=minio-client-app \
          client_secret=minio-client-app-secret \
          config_url="http://localhost:5556/dex/.well-known/openid-configuration" \
          scopes="openid,groups" \
          redirect_uri="http://127.0.0.1:10000/oauth_callback" \
          role_policy="consoleAdmin"
  2. Create OpenID IDP configuration named "dex_test".
     $ @PROG@ idp openid add play/ dex_test \
          client_id=minio-client-app \
          client_secret=minio-client-app-secret \
          config_url="http://localhost:5556/dex/.well-known/openid-configuration" \
          scopes="openid,groups" \
          redirect_uri="http://127.0.0.1:10000/oauth_callback" \
          role_policy="consoleAdmin"

=== help idp openid accesskey list
NAME:
  @PROG@ idp openid accesskey list - list access key pairs for OpenID

USAGE:
  @PROG@ idp openid accesskey list [FLAGS] TARGET[:CFGNAME] [USER/ID...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Get list of all OpenID users and associated access keys in local server (if admin)
    $ @PROG@ idp openid accesskey list local/

  2. Get list of OpenID users in local server (if admin)
    $ @PROG@ idp openid accesskey list local/ --users-only

  3. Get list of all users and associated temporary access keys in play server (if admin)
   $ @PROG@ idp openid accesskey list play/ --temp-only

  4. Get list of access keys associated with internal name 'openidinternalname'
     $ @PROG@ idp openid accesskey list play/ openidinternalname

  5. Get list of access keys associated with ID claim 'openidsub' (default claim is sub)
   $ @PROG@ idp openid accesskey list play/ openidsub

  7. Get authenticated user and associated access keys in local server (if not admin)
   $ @PROG@ idp openid accesskey list local/

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:

     $ @PROG@ idp ldap add myminio/ \
          server_addr=myldapserver:636 \
          lookup_bind_dn=cn=admin,dc=min,dc=io \
          lookup_bind_password=somesecret \
          user_dn_search_base_dn=dc=min,dc=io \
          user_dn_search_filter="(uid=%s)" \
          group_search_base_dn=ou=swengg,dc=min,dc=io \
          group_search_filter="(&(objectclass=groupofnames)(member=%d))"

=== help idp ldap policy entities
NAME:
  @PROG@ idp ldap policy entities - list policy association entities

USAGE:
  @PROG@ idp ldap policy entities [FLAGS] TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. List all LDAP entities associated with all policies
     $ @PROG@ idp ldap policy entities play/
  2. List all LDAP entities associated with the policies 'finteam-policy' and 'mlteam-policy'
     $ @PROG@ idp ldap policy entities play/ --policy finteam-policy --policy mlteam-policy
  3. List all policies associated with a pair of User LDAP entities
     $ @PROG@ idp ldap policy entities play/ \
              --user 'uid=bobfisher,ou=people,ou=hwengg,dc=min,dc=io' \
              --user 'uid=fahim,ou=people,ou=swengg,dc=min,dc=io'
  4. List all policies associated with a pair of Group LDAP entities
     $ @PROG@ idp ldap policy entities play/ \
              --group 'cn=projecta,ou=groups,ou=swengg,dc=min,dc=io' \
              --group 'cn=projectb,ou=groups,ou=swengg,dc=min,dc=io'
  5. List all entities associated with a policy, group and user
     $ @PROG@ idp ldap policy entities play/ \
              --policy finteam-policy
              --user 'uid=bobfisher,ou=people,ou=hwengg,dc=min,dc=io' \
              --group 'cn=projectb,ou=groups,ou=swengg,dc=min,dc=io'

=== help idp ldap accesskey list
NAME:
  @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey list - list access key pairs for LDAP

USAGE:
  @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey list [FLAGS] TARGET [DN...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Get list of all LDAP users and associated access keys in local server (if admin)
    $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey list local/

  2. Get list of LDAP users in local server (if admin)
    $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey list local/ --users-only

  3. Get list of all users and associated temporary access keys in play server (if admin)
   $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey list play/ --temp-only

  4. Get list of access keys associated with user 'bobfisher'
     $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey list play/ uid=bobfisher,dc=min,dc=io

  5. Get list of access keys associated with user 'bobfisher' (alt)
   $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey list play/ bobfisher

  6. Get list of access keys associated with users 'bobfisher' and 'cody3'
     $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey list play/ uid=bobfisher,dc=min,dc=io uid=cody3,dc=min,dc=io

  7. Get authenticated user and associated access keys in local server (if not admin)
   $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey list local/

@FLAGS:2@

   $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey info local/ testkey
  2. Get info for the access keys "testkey" and "testkey2"
   $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey info local/ testkey testkey2

=== help idp ldap accesskey create
NAME:
  @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey create - create access key pairs for LDAP

USAGE:
  @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey create [FLAGS] [TARGET]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Create a new access key pair with the same policy as the authenticated user
     $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey create local/

  2. Create a new access key pair with custom access key and secret key
     $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey create local/ --access-key myaccesskey --secret-key mysecretkey

  4. Create a new access key pair for user with username "james" that expires in 1 day
     $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey create local/ james --expiry-duration 24h

  5. Create a new access key pair for authenticated user that expires on 2021-01-01
     $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey create --expiry 2021-01-01

=== help idp ldap accesskey sts-revoke
NAME:
  @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey sts-revoke - revokes all STS accounts or specified types for the specified user

USAGE:
  @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey sts-revoke ALIAS USER [--all | --token-type TOKEN_TYPE]

  Exactly one of --all or --token-type must be specified.

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Revoke all STS accounts for LDAP user 'bobfisher'
   $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey sts-revoke myminio uid=bobfisher,ou=people,ou=hwengg,dc=min,dc=io --all

  2. Revoke all STS accounts for LDAP user 'bobfisher' (alt)
   $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey sts-revoke myminio bobfisher --all

  3. Revoke STS accounts of a token type 'app-1' for user 'user1'
   $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey sts-revoke myminio user1 --token-type app-1

  4. Revoke all STS accounts for the authenticated user (must be LDAP service account)
   $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey sts-revoke myminio --self

  5. Revoke STS accounts of a token type 'app-1' for the authenticated user (must be LDAP service account)
   $ @PROG@ idp ldap accesskey sts-revoke myminio --self --token-type app-1

=== help ls
NAME:
  @PROG@ ls - list buckets and objects

USAGE:
  @PROG@ ls [FLAGS] TARGET [TARGET ...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. List buckets on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ @PROG@ ls s3

  2. List buckets and all its contents from Amazon S3 cloud storage recursively.
     $ @PROG@ ls --recursive s3

  3. List all contents of mybucket on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ @PROG@ ls s3/mybucket/

  4. List all contents of mybucket on Amazon S3 cloud storage on Microsoft Windows.
     $ @PROG@ ls s3\mybucket\

  5. List files recursively on a local filesystem on Microsoft Windows.
     $ @PROG@ ls --recursive C:\Users\Worf\

  6. List incomplete (previously failed) uploads of objects on Amazon S3.
     $ @PROG@ ls --incomplete s3/mybucket

  7. List contents at a specific time in the past if the bucket versioning is enabled.
     $ @PROG@ ls --rewind 2020.01.01 s3/mybucket
     $ @PROG@ ls --rewind 2020.01.01T11:30 s3/mybucket
     $ @PROG@ ls --rewind 7d s3/mybucket

  8. List all contents versions if the bucket versioning is enabled.
     $ @PROG@ ls --versions s3/mybucket

  9. List all objects on mybucket, summarize the number of objects and total size.
     $ @PROG@ ls --summarize s3/mybucket/
  
  10. List all objects on mybucket, for the GLACIER storage class
     $ @PROG@ ls --storage-class 'GLACIER' s3/mybucket

=== help mb
NAME:
  @PROG@ mb - make a bucket

USAGE:
  @PROG@ mb [FLAGS] TARGET [TARGET...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Create a bucket on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ @PROG@ mb s3/mynewbucket

  2. Create a new bucket on Google Cloud Storage.
     $ @PROG@ mb gcs/miniocloud

  3. Create a new bucket on Amazon S3 cloud storage in region 'us-west-2'.
     $ @PROG@ mb --region=us-west-2 s3/myregionbucket

  4. Create a new directory including its missing parents (equivalent to 'mkdir -p').
     $ @PROG@ mb /tmp/this/new/dir1

  5. Create multiple directories including its missing parents (behavior similar to 'mkdir -p').
     $ @PROG@ mb /mnt/sdb/mydisk /mnt/sdc/mydisk /mnt/sdd/mydisk

  6. Ignore if bucket/directory already exists.
     $ @PROG@ mb --ignore-existing myminio/mynewbucket

  7. Create a new bucket on Amazon S3 cloud storage in region 'us-west-2' with object lock enabled.
     $ @PROG@ mb --with-lock --region=us-west-2 s3/myregionbucket

  8. Create a new bucket on MinIO with versioning enabled.
     $ @PROG@ mb --with-versioning myminio/myversionedbucket

--enc-kms value                    encrypt/decrypt objects using specific server-side encryption keys. (multiple keys can be provided) [$MC_ENC_KMS]

=== help mv
NAME:
  @PROG@ mv - move objects

USAGE:
  @PROG@ mv [FLAGS] SOURCE [SOURCE...] TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES:
  MC_ENC_KMS: KMS encryption key in the form of (alias/prefix=key).
  MC_ENC_S3: S3 encryption key in the form of (alias/prefix=key).

EXAMPLES:
  01. Move a list of objects from local file system to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mv Music/*.ogg s3/jukebox/

  02. Move a folder recursively from MinIO cloud storage to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mv --recursive play/mybucket/ s3/mybucket/

  03. Move multiple local folders recursively to MinIO cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mv --recursive backup/2014/ backup/2015/ play/archive/

  04. Move a bucket recursively from aliased Amazon S3 cloud storage to local filesystem on Windows.
      $ @PROG@ mv --recursive s3\documents\2014\ C:\Backups\2014

  05. Move files older than 7 days and 10 hours from MinIO cloud storage to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mv --older-than 7d10h play/mybucket/myfolder/ s3/mybucket/

  06. Move files newer than 7 days and 10 hours from MinIO cloud storage to a local path.
      $ @PROG@ mv --newer-than 7d10h play/mybucket/myfolder/ ~/latest/

  07. Move an object with name containing unicode characters to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mv 本語 s3/andoria/

  08. Move a local folder with space separated characters to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mv --recursive 'workdir/documents/May 2014/' s3/miniocloud

  09. Move a list of objects from local file system to MinIO cloud storage with specified metadata, separated by ";"
      $ @PROG@ mv --attr "key1=value1;key2=value2" Music/*.mp4 play/mybucket/

  10. Move a list of objects from local file system to MinIO cloud storage and set tags to the uploaded objects
      $ @PROG@ mv --tag "key1=value1" Music/*.mp4 play/mybucket/

  11. Move a folder recursively from MinIO cloud storage to Amazon S3 cloud storage with Cache-Control and custom metadata, separated by ";".
      $ @PROG@ mv --attr "Cache-Control=max-age=90000,min-fresh=9000;key1=value1;key2=value2" --recursive play/mybucket/myfolder/ s3/mybucket/

  12. Move a text file to an object storage and assign REDUCED_REDUNDANCY storage-class to the uploaded object.
      $ @PROG@ mv --storage-class REDUCED_REDUNDANCY myobject.txt play/mybucket

  13. Move a text file to an object storage and preserve the file system attribute as metadata.
      $ @PROG@ mv -a myobject.txt play/mybucket

  14. Move a text file to an object storage and disable multipart upload feature.
      $ @PROG@ mv --disable-multipart myobject.txt play/mybucket

  15. Move a folder using client provided encryption keys from Amazon S3 to MinIO cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mv --r --enc-c "s3/documents/=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5MBB" --enc-c "myminio/documents/=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5MDA" s3/documents/ myminio/documents/

  16. Move a folder using specific server managed encryption keys from Amazon S3 to MinIO cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mv --r --enc-s3 "s3/documents" --enc-s3 "myminio/documents" s3/documents/ myminio/documents/

  17. Add SHA256 checksum to move a text file to MinIO cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mv --checksum SHA256 myobject.txt play/mybucket

=== flags mirror

=== help mirror
NAME:
  @PROG@ mirror - synchronize object(s) to a remote site

USAGE:
  @PROG@ mirror [FLAGS] SOURCE TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES:
  MC_ENC_KMS: KMS encryption key in the form of (alias/prefix=key).
  MC_ENC_S3: S3 encryption key in the form of (alias/prefix=key).

EXAMPLES:
  01. Mirror a bucket recursively from MinIO cloud storage to a bucket on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mirror play/photos/2014 s3/backup-photos

  02. Mirror a local folder recursively to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mirror backup/ s3/archive

  03. Only mirror files that are newer than 7 days, 10 hours and 30 minutes to Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mirror --newer-than "7d10h30m" backup/ s3/archive

  04. Mirror a bucket from aliased Amazon S3 cloud storage to a folder on Windows.
      $ @PROG@ mirror s3\documents\2014\ C:\backup\2014

  05. Mirror a bucket from aliased Amazon S3 cloud storage to a local folder use '--overwrite' to overwrite destination.
      $ @PROG@ mirror --overwrite s3/miniocloud miniocloud-backup

  06. Mirror a bucket from MinIO cloud storage to a bucket on Amazon S3 cloud storage and remove any extraneous
      files on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mirror --remove play/photos/2014 s3/backup-photos/2014

  07. Continuously mirror a local folder recursively to MinIO cloud storage. '--watch' continuously watches for
      new objects, uploads and removes extraneous files on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ mirror --remove --watch /var/lib/backups play/backups

  08. Continuously mirror all buckets and objects from site 1 to site 2, removed buckets and objects will be reflected as well.
      $ @PROG@ mirror --remove --watch site1-alias/ site2-alias/

  09. Mirror a bucket from aliased Amazon S3 cloud storage to a local folder.
      Exclude all .* files and *.temp files when mirroring.
      $ @PROG@ mirror --exclude ".*" --exclude "*.temp" s3/test ~/test

  10. Mirror all buckets from aliased Amazon S3 cloud storage to a local folder.
      Exclude test* buckets and backup* buckets when mirroring.
      $ @PROG@ mirror --exclude-bucket 'test*' --exclude 'backup*' s3 ~/test

  11. Mirror objects newer than 10 days from bucket test to a local folder.
      $ @PROG@ mirror --newer-than 10d s3/test ~/localfolder

  12. Mirror objects older than 30 days from Amazon S3 bucket test to a local folder.
      $ @PROG@ mirror --older-than 30d s3/test ~/test

  13. Mirror server encrypted objects from Amazon S3 cloud storage to a bucket on Amazon S3 cloud storage
      $ @PROG@ mirror --enc-c "minio/archive=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5MDA" --enc-c "s3/archive=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5BBB" s3/archive/ minio/archive/ 

  14. Update 'Cache-Control' header on all existing objects recursively.
      $ @PROG@ mirror --attr "Cache-Control=max-age=90000,min-fresh=9000" myminio/video-files myminio/video-files

  15. Mirror a local folder recursively to Amazon S3 cloud storage and preserve all local file attributes.
      $ @PROG@ mirror -a backup/ s3/archive

  16. Cross mirror between sites in a active-active deployment.
      Site-A: $ @PROG@ mirror --active-active siteA siteB
      Site-B: $ @PROG@ mirror --active-active siteB siteA

=== help od
NAME:
  @PROG@ od - measure single stream upload and download

USAGE:
  @PROG@ od [OPERANDS]

OPERANDS:
  if=        source stream to upload
  of=        target path to upload to
  size=      size of each part. If not specified, will be calculated from the source stream size.
  parts=     number of parts to upload. If not specified, will calculated from the source file size.
  skip=      number of parts to skip.

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Upload 200MiB of a file to a bucket in 5 parts of size 40MiB.
      @PROG@ od if=file.txt of=play/my-bucket/file.txt size=40MiB parts=5

  2. Upload a full file to a bucket with 40MiB parts.
      @PROG@ od if=file.txt of=play/my-bucket/file.txt size=40MiB

  3. Upload a full file to a bucket in 5 parts.
      @PROG@ od if=file.txt of=play/my-bucket/file.txt parts=5

USAGE:
  @PROG@ ping [FLAGS] TARGET [TARGET...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Return Latency and liveness probe.
     $ @PROG@ ping myminio

  2. Return Latency and liveness probe 5 number of times.

  3. Return Latency and liveness with wait interval set to 30 seconds.
     $ @PROG@ ping --interval 30 myminio

  4. Stop pinging when error count > 20.
     $ @PROG@ ping --error-count 20 myminio

=== help pipe
NAME:
  @PROG@ pipe - stream STDIN to an object

USAGE:
  @PROG@ pipe [FLAGS] [TARGET]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES:
  MC_ENC_KMS: KMS encryption key in the form of (alias/prefix=key).
  MC_ENC_S3: S3 encryption key in the form of (alias/prefix=key).

EXAMPLES:
  1. Write contents of stdin to a file on local filesystem.
     $ @PROG@ pipe /tmp/hello-world.go

  2. Write contents of stdin to an object on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ @PROG@ pipe s3/personalbuck/meeting-notes.txt

  3. Copy an ISO image to an object on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ cat debian-8.2.iso | @PROG@ pipe s3/opensource-isos/gnuos.iso

  4. Copy an ISO image to an object on minio storage using KMS encryption.
     $ cat debian-8.2.iso | @PROG@ pipe --enc-kms="minio/opensource-isos=my-key-name" minio/opensource-isos/gnuos.iso

  5. Stream MySQL database dump to Amazon S3 directly.
     $ mysqldump -u root -p ******* accountsdb | @PROG@ pipe s3/sql-backups/backups/accountsdb-oct-9-2015.sql

  6. Write contents of stdin to an object on Amazon S3 cloud storage and assign REDUCED_REDUNDANCY storage-class to the uploaded object.
     $ @PROG@ pipe --storage-class REDUCED_REDUNDANCY s3/personalbuck/meeting-notes.txt

  7. Copy to MinIO cloud storage with specified metadata, separated by ";"
      $ cat music.mp3 | @PROG@ pipe --attr "Cache-Control=max-age=90000,min-fresh=9000;Artist=Unknown" play/mybucket/music.mp3

  8. Set tags to the uploaded objects
      $ tar cvf - . | @PROG@ pipe --tags "category=prod&type=backup" play/mybucket/backup.tar

=== help quota set
NAME:
  @PROG@ quota set - set bucket quota

USAGE:
  @PROG@ quota set TARGET [--size QUOTA]

QUOTA
  Quota accepts human-readable case-insensitive number.
  Suffixes such as "k", "m", "g" and "t" referring to the metric units KB,
  MB, GB and TB respectively. Adding an "i" to these prefixes, uses the IEC
  units, so that "gi" refers to "gibibyte" or "GiB". A "b" at the end is
  also accepted. Without suffixes the unit is bytes.

  The MinIO object scanner checks a bucket's quota each time it is scanned.
  If the scanner determines a bucket has met or exceeded its quota, MinIO
  rejects subsequent object write requests until the scanner determines the
  bucket no longer exceeds its quota.

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Set hard quota of 1gb for a bucket "mybucket" on MinIO.
     $ @PROG@ quota set myminio/mybucket --size 1GB

=== flags quota info

=== flags rm
--versions                       remove object(s) and all its versions

--force                          allow a recursive remove operation
--dangerous                      allow site-wide removal of objects

--version-id value, --vid value  delete a specific version of an object
--incomplete, -I                 remove incomplete uploads
--dry-run                        perform a fake remove operation
--stdin                          read object names from STDIN
--older-than value               remove objects older than value in duration string (e.g. 7d10h31s)
--newer-than value               remove objects newer than value in duration string (e.g. 7d10h31s)
--bypass                         bypass governance
--non-current                    remove object(s) versions that are non-current

=== help rm
NAME:
  @PROG@ rm - remove object(s)

USAGE:
  @PROG@ rm [FLAGS] TARGET [TARGET ...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

EXAMPLES:
  01. Remove a file.
      $ @PROG@ rm 1999/old-backup.tgz

  02. Perform a fake remove operation.
      $ @PROG@ rm --dry-run 1999/old-backup.tgz

  03. Remove all objects recursively from bucket 'jazz-songs' matching the prefix 'louis'.
      $ @PROG@ rm --recursive --force s3/jazz-songs/louis/

  04. Remove all objects older than '90' days recursively from bucket 'jazz-songs' matching the prefix 'louis'.
      $ @PROG@ rm --recursive --force --older-than 90d s3/jazz-songs/louis/

  05. Remove all objects newer than 7 days and 10 hours recursively from bucket 'pop-songs'
      $ @PROG@ rm --recursive --force --newer-than 7d10h s3/pop-songs/

  06. Remove all objects read from STDIN.
      $ @PROG@ rm --force --stdin

  07. Remove all objects recursively from Amazon S3 cloud storage.
      $ @PROG@ rm --recursive --force --dangerous s3

  08. Remove all objects older than '90' days recursively under all buckets.
      $ @PROG@ rm --recursive --dangerous --force --older-than 90d s3

  09. Drop all incomplete uploads on the bucket 'jazz-songs'.
      $ @PROG@ rm --incomplete --recursive --force s3/jazz-songs/

  10. Bypass object retention in governance mode and delete the object.
      $ @PROG@ rm --bypass s3/pop-songs/

  11. Remove a particular version ID.
      $ @PROG@ rm s3/docs/money.xls --version-id "f20f3792-4bd4-4288-8d3c-b9d05b3b62f6"

  12. Remove all object versions older than one year.
      $ @PROG@ rm s3/docs/ --recursive --versions --rewind 365d

  14. Perform a fake removal of object(s) versions that are non-current and older than 10 days. If top-level version is a delete 
  marker, this will also be deleted when --non-current flag is specified.
      $ @PROG@ rm s3/docs/ --recursive --force --versions --non-current --older-than 10d --dry-run

=== help retention set
NAME:
  @PROG@ retention set - apply retention settings on object(s)

USAGE:
  @PROG@ retention set [FLAGS] [governance | compliance] VALIDITY TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
VALIDITY:
  This argument must be formatted like Nd or Ny where 'd' denotes days and 'y' denotes years e.g. 10d, 3y.

EXAMPLES:
  1. Set object retention for a specific object
     $ @PROG@ retention set compliance 30d myminio/mybucket/prefix/obj.csv

  2. Set object retention for recursively for all objects at a given prefix
     $ @PROG@ retention set governance 30d myminio/mybucket/prefix --recursive

  3. Set object retention to a specific version of a specific object
     $ @PROG@ retention set governance 30d myminio/mybucket/prefix/obj.csv --version-id "3Jr2x6fqlBUsVzbvPihBO3HgNpgZgAnp"

  4. Set object retention for recursively for all versions of all objects
     $ @PROG@ retention set governance 30d myminio/mybucket/prefix --recursive --versions

  5. Set default lock retention configuration for a bucket
     $ @PROG@ retention set --default governance 30d myminio/mybucket/

=== help replicate add
NAME:
  @PROG@ replicate add - add a server side replication configuration rule

USAGE:
  @PROG@ replicate add TARGET

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Add replication configuration rule on bucket "sourcebucket" for alias "sourceminio" with alias "targetminio" to replicate all operations in an active-active replication setup.
     $ @PROG@ replicate add sourceminio/sourcebucket --remote-bucket targetminio/targetbucket \
         --priority 1 

  2. Add replication configuration rule on bucket "mybucket" for alias "myminio" to replicate all operations in an active-active replication setup.
     $ @PROG@ replicate add myminio/mybucket --remote-bucket https://foobar:foo12345@minio.siteb.example.com/targetbucket \
         --priority 1 

  3. Add replication configuration rule on bucket "mybucket" for alias "myminio" to replicate all objects with tags
     "key1=value1, key2=value2" to targetbucket synchronously with bandwidth set to 2 gigabits per second. 
     $ @PROG@ replicate add myminio/mybucket --remote-bucket https://foobar:foo12345@minio.siteb.example.com/targetbucket  \
         --tags "key1=value1&key2=value2" --bandwidth "2G" --sync \
         --priority 1

  4. Disable a replication configuration rule on bucket "mybucket" for alias "myminio".
     $ @PROG@ replicate add myminio/mybucket --remote-bucket https://foobar:foo12345@minio.siteb.example.com/targetbucket  \
         --tags "key1=value1&key2=value2" \
         --priority 1 --disable

  5. Add replication configuration rule with existing object replication, delete marker replication and versioned deletes
     enabled on bucket "mybucket" for alias "myminio".
     $ @PROG@ replicate add myminio/mybucket --remote-bucket https://foobar:foo12345@minio.siteb.example.com/targetbucket  \
         --replicate "existing-objects,delete,delete-marker" \
         --priority 1

--priority value                 priority of the rule, should be unique and is a required field (default: 0)
--remote-bucket value            destination bucket, should be a unique value for the configuration
--replicate value                comma separated list to enable replication of soft deletes, permanent deletes, existing objects and metadata sync. Valid options are "delete-marker","delete","existing-objects","metadata-sync" and ""'
--sync value                     enable synchronous replication for this target, valid values are ['enable', 'disable']. (default: "disable")
--proxy value                    enable proxying in active-active replication, valid values are ['enable', 'disable'] (default: "enable")
--bandwidth value                Set bandwidth limit in bytes per second (K,B,G,T for metric and Ki,Bi,Gi,Ti for IEC units)
--healthcheck-seconds value      health check duration in seconds (default: 60)
--path value                     bucket path lookup supported by the server, valid options are ['on', 'off', 'auto'] (default: "auto")
--help, -h                       show help
=== help replicate update
NAME:
  @PROG@ replicate update - modify an existing server side replication configuration rule

USAGE:
  @PROG@ replicate update TARGET --id=RULE-ID [FLAGS]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  
EXAMPLES:
  1. Change priority of rule with rule ID "bsibgh8t874dnjst8hkg" on bucket "mybucket" for alias "myminio".
     $ @PROG@ replicate update myminio/mybucket --id "bsibgh8t874dnjst8hkg"  --priority 3

  2. Disable a replication configuration rule with rule ID "bsibgh8t874dnjst8hkg" on target myminio/bucket
     $ @PROG@ replicate update myminio/mybucket --id "bsibgh8t874dnjst8hkg" --state disable

  3. Set tags and storage class on a replication configuration with rule ID "kMYD.491" on target myminio/bucket/prefix.
     $ @PROG@ replicate update myminio/mybucket --id "kMYD.491" --tags "key1=value1&key2=value2" \
          --storage-class "STANDARD" --priority 2
  4. Clear tags for replication configuration rule with ID "kMYD.491" on a target myminio/bucket.
     $ @PROG@ replicate update myminio/mybucket --id "kMYD.491" --tags ""

  5. Enable delete marker replication on a replication configuration rule with ID "kxYD.491" on a target myminio/bucket.
     $ @PROG@ replicate update myminio/mybucket --id "kxYD.491" --replicate "delete-marker"

  6. Disable delete marker and versioned delete replication on a replication configuration rule with ID "kxYD.491" on a target myminio/bucket.
     $ @PROG@ replicate update myminio/mybucket --id "kxYD.491" --replicate ""

  7. Enable existing object replication on a configuration rule with ID "kxYD.491" on a target myminio/bucket. Rule previously had enabled delete marker and versioned delete replication.
     $ @PROG@ replicate update myminio/mybucket --id "kxYD.491" --replicate "existing-objects,delete-marker,delete"

  8. Edit credentials for remote target with replication rule ID kxYD.491
     $ @PROG@ replicate update myminio/mybucket --id "kxYD.491" --remote-bucket  https://foobar:newpassword@minio.siteb.example.com/targetbucket
  
  9. Edit credentials with alias "targetminio" for remote target with replication rule ID kxYD.491
     $ @PROG@ replicate update myminio/mybucket --id "kxYD.491" --remote-bucket  targetminio/targetbucket

  10. Disable proxying and enable synchronous replication for remote target of bucket mybucket with rule ID kxYD.492
     $ @PROG@ replicate update myminio/mybucket --id "kxYD.492" --remote-bucket https://foobar:newpassword@minio.siteb.example.com/targetbucket \
         --sync "enable" --proxy "disable"

=== help sql
NAME:
  @PROG@ sql - run sql queries on objects

USAGE:
  @PROG@ sql [FLAGS] TARGET [TARGET...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

SERIALIZATION OPTIONS:
  For query serialization options, refer to https://docs.min.io/community/minio-object-store/reference/minio-mc/mc-sql.html

EXAMPLES:
  1. Run a query on a set of objects recursively on AWS S3.
     $ @PROG@ sql --recursive --query "select * from S3Object" s3/personalbucket/my-large-csvs/

  2. Run a query on an object on MinIO.
     $ @PROG@ sql --query "select count(s.power) from S3Object s" myminio/iot-devices/power-ratio.csv

  3. Run a query on an encrypted object with customer provided keys.
     $ @PROG@ sql --enc-c "myminio/iot-devices=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5MDA" \
         --query "select count(s.power) from S3Object s" myminio/iot-devices/power-ratio-encrypted.csv

  4. Run a query on an object on MinIO in gzip format using ; as field delimiter,
     newline as record delimiter and file header to be used
     $ @PROG@ sql --compression GZIP --csv-input "rd=\n,fh=USE,fd=;" \
         --query "select count(s.power) from S3Object s" myminio/iot-devices/power-ratio.csv.gz

  5. Run a query on an object on MinIO in gzip format using ; as field delimiter,
     newline as record delimiter and file header to be used
     $ @PROG@ sql --compression GZIP --csv-input "rd=\n,fh=USE,fd=;" \
         --json-output "rd=\n\n" --query "select * from S3Object" myminio/iot-devices/data.csv

  6. Run same query as in 5., but specify csv output headers. If --csv-output-headers is
     specified as "", first row of csv is interpreted as header
     $ @PROG@ sql --compression GZIP --csv-input "rd=\n,fh=USE,fd=;" \
         --csv-output "rd=\n" --csv-output-header "device_id,uptime,lat,lon" \
         --query "select * from S3Object" myminio/iot-devices/data.csv

=== help stat
NAME:
  @PROG@ stat - show object metadata

USAGE:
  @PROG@ stat [FLAGS] TARGET [TARGET ...]

FLAGS:
@FLAGS:2@
  

EXAMPLES:
  1. Stat all contents of mybucket on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ @PROG@ stat s3/mybucket/

  2. Stat all contents of all buckets on Amazon S3 cloud storage.
     $ @PROG@ stat s3 --verbose

  3. Stat all contents of mybucket on Amazon S3 cloud storage on Microsoft Windows.
     $ @PROG@ stat s3\mybucket\

  4. Stat files recursively on a local filesystem on Microsoft Windows.
     $ @PROG@ stat --recursive C:\Users\mydocuments\

  5. Stat encrypted files on Amazon S3 cloud storage. In case the encryption key contains non-printable character like tab, pass the
     base64 encoded string as key.
     $ @PROG@ stat --enc-c "s3/personal-document/=MDEyMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0NTY3ODkwMTIzNDU2Nzg5MDA" s3/personal-document/2019-account_report.docx

  6. Stat a specific object version.
     $ @PROG@ stat --version-id "CL3sWgdSN2pNntSf6UnZAuh2kcu8E8si" s3/personal-docs/2018-account_report.docx

  7. Stat all objects versions recursively created before 1st January 2020.
     $ @PROG@ stat --versions --rewind 2020.01.01T00:00 s3/personal-docs/
